newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end down after specs trigger stops.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end down after specs trigger stops.

text.p: FCOJ July futures continued to drift lower amid technically-driven selling that pressured the benchmark July contract to a one-week low, dealers said.
The market recorded early losses on follow-through selling from Friday. Stops were triggered around 77.00 cents, pressuring the July contract to 76.50 cents, the low hit on June 2.
Light short-covering by the trade and locals kept the spot month from falling to support around 76.00 cents, where traders are likely to uncover additional stops.

The benchmark July contract closed 0.90 cent lower at 76.90 cents per lb, having ranged from 77.75 to 76.50 cents. September finished down 0.80 at 79.30 cents, while the remaining months settled 0.60 lower to 0.05 firmer.
Volume was estimated at 2,500 lots compared with Friday's official 2,181 lots.
The fundamentals, meanwhile, remain bearish. "We had stories last week about the Medfly and the canker but no one is really concerned," Celeste Georgakis, vice president with Dean Witter, said.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture will release its estimate of the 1996/97 Florida crop on June 12. Market sources expect no revision to the current estimate.
The USDA put Florida's crop at a record 224.2 million 90-lb boxes and yields at 1.58 gallons per box.
